title: LIBS 7102 · Lecture 4
subtitle: Act utilitarianism I: from relativism to theories, the hats of hacking, Bentham, equal consideration of interests, the felicific calculus, Mill, the utilitarian procedure, and Jim, the trolley, the fat man, Strangelove and Andy
description: Lecture 4 of LIBS 7102: why rejecting relativism needs a normative theory and why "it depends" is not relativism; white, black and grey hats and what utilitarianism looks at; Bentham's two sovereign masters, psychological and normative hedonism and the principle of utility; equal consideration of interests and the five-person row, not the majority; the seven dimensions of the felicific calculus and why no kind of action is wrong in itself; Mill's four changes, the Greatest Happiness Principle read correctly, the competent judges and the proof; how a utilitarian can know what to do; Williams's Jim, the trolley, the fat man, Strangelove's ICBM and Andy's lie, each put to you before the verdict. Practice answer U3 and a 20-item mock quiz.
intro:
:::exam Midterm facts
**Midterm: Wednesday Oct 28, in class.** Closed book, two hours, on paper, 20 % of the course. You write four or five two-paragraph answers, choosing from about six (for example, answer 4 of 6). Questions cover lectures 1 to 5 and are taken from the practice list (rare) or very similar to it (typical), often paired with a computing case or asking you to argue a side. With Lecture 5 it feeds fifteen of the twenty-five listed practice questions, usually three of the six questions on the paper.
:::

lessons.title: Rejecting relativism leaves open which theory tells you what to do
White, black and grey hats differ by permission and intent; utilitarianism looks only at outcomes
Bentham: pleasure and pain are our two sovereign masters, and utility is the test of right
Equal consideration counts everyone's interests equally; it does not treat everyone equally
Bentham measures pleasure on seven dimensions, so no kind of action is wrong in itself
Mill adds quality to pleasure and a proof, and judges concrete actions
Right means maximizing actual utility, a test of actions, not a decision procedure
Jim and the twenty: Williams offers Jim one prisoner to shoot, or Pedro kills all twenty
The trolley, the fat man, Strangelove and Andy: utilitarianism makes the outcome decide
